Subject: Re: RDW-9843 — initial capacity inputs for Dedicated sizing

Maya — thanks, great summary. See our sizing assumptions below (conservative by design):

- Target p90 latency: 120ms (production SLA target)
- Steady-state concurrency: 1200 sessions (average), spike up to 3,000 concurrent sessions
- Steady QPS: ~600 qps average, spike 1,500 qps (10–30s bursts)
- Typical sequence: 256 tokens prompt / 512 tokens completion (max combined 1024)
- Preferred HW mapping: primary = A100 80GB or equivalent; fallback = H100 80GB (note perf deltas below)
- Constraints: US regions only for initial deploy; private/VPC deployment required for this customer

From these numbers, ballpark we see a dedicated pool of 18 A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs to meet p90 for sustained throughput with modest batching (~4–6x). If OEMs cannot deliver A100s in time, a hybrid plan with 12 H100 nodes + cloud burst capacity is viable but will require quantization/throughput tuning and a short regression window.

I've attached Redwood_Dedicated_specs_v2.pdf which includes model memory/KV-cache expectations, batching guidance, and expected token-level cost at different batch sizes.

Next asks:
- Can Nimbus obtain formal ETA and MOQ pricing from GPUOMEX and a second OEM?
- Can Nimbus tentatively hold burstable capacity for us for 8 weeks after PO?
- We'll need OEM lead-time + expedite fees to decide on an upfront deposit vs. cloud-bridge approach.

I'll coordinate procurement and engineering touchpoints. Vivek — tagging you for procurement policy & expedite approvals. Dev — can you confirm the performance multiplier you used earlier for H100->A100 equivalence?

Best,
Olga Petrov

Subject: Internal: RDW-9843 — recommended bridge & procurement playbook

Team — quick internal note (engineering + procurement POV):

1) Bridge approach (recommended):
   - Short term (0–8 weeks): Disable large-batch prefilling and rely on Nimbus burst instances (managed) for peak spikes. Reserve 12 H100-equivalent GPUs as immediate capacity (covering ~65% of steady state).
   - Medium term (8–20 weeks): Accept partial A100 shipments when available to reach 18-unit target. Use auto-rollout with canary set to A100 nodes.
   - Fallback: If A100 delays >20 weeks, convert to full H100 fleet and increase batching while adjusting p90 SLA (communicated to customer).

2) Procurement checklist:
   - Approve expedite fee threshold (I recommend <15% of lineitem cost) — Olga to confirm with customer/finance.
   - Authorize deposit up to 25% to secure vendor priority (requires VP approval).
   - Negotiate partial ship + acceptance criteria for early test units (4-unit partial shipment).

3) Engineering actions:
   - Dev: run a 48-hour regression on H100 with quantized runtime and the sample workload (dev, please confirm ETA 72 hours).
   - Ops: instrument KV-cache metrics and token-latency dashboards for the canary window.

Olga — once you confirm deposit stance with the customer, I'll draft a PO template and expedite approval flow.

— Vivek
